steps.path: Setup wizard, the between-sessions screen, the tour, tips, Projects, Settings and the first warnings
steps.headline: The contract, graded — accept these verdicts?

rows.statement: The buddy stands in a corner of the real app with a speech bubble that points at the control each stop is about.
rows.note: but i think i do want to add a line to the system prompt or a new tool to better allow the assistant to view/explain it's own capabilities. "If a user asks you how to do x or y or about how youcoded works or its settings menus, use *youcoded-info-desk* to answer. this can be roadmapped for now.
rows.evidence: rebuilt branch: docs/archive/design/2026-09-10-first-run-guide/runs/after/shots-guide/midnight/tour-1.png and light/tour-1.png, beside the approved crop docs/archive/design/2026-09-10-first-run-guide/images/first-run-guide.review/tour-1--midnight--after.png; bubble in the bottom-right corner, ring drawn by GuideRing on the stop's anchor (stop 2 rings the form, stop 6 the providers list)

rows.statement: The tour starts on its own once, right after setup; Show me around in Settings brings it back any time.
rows.evidence: npx vitest run youcoded/desktop/tests/first-run-guide.test.tsx — 9 passed — 'owes a tour only after the wizard hands off, and settles it on done'; Show me around is App.tsx's onShowMeAround → setTourOpen(true)

rows.statement: Every stop is a sentence or two and Next; a stop with an obvious action also offers a button that does it.
rows.note: should also open some settings pages and projects view so the user can see what the assistant is talking about as it explains.

rows.statement: The tour has eight stops in this order: buddy, sessions, projects, models and providers, tags and notes, files, make it yours, help.
The sentence about the assistant changing and deleting files lives on the setup wizard, where nobody can skip past it.
rows.note: that reminds me. as part of this work, i also want to add some clearer warnings/popups the first time some things are done. like when a user enables skip permissions or full auto, or uses a small small model for the first time (like 9b-40b class) we should very cleary explain that these actions are more likely to result in damage and data loss, especially when used with less capable models. we should be honest without being scary, so a user just has pragmatic expectations. full auto and skip permissions should require a "i understand" checkbox with a continue button. just want to cover our asses for obvious liability issues

rows.note: "With your permission, the assistant may create, change, or delete files on your device. Create backups for anything you cannot replace.

rows.statement: These are the eight tips, each fired by its named moment: tags, notes, projects, resume, local models, buddy floater, themes, help.

rows.statement: The word "artifacts" is gone from the empty Projects screen; once a project exists, the screen is today's again.
rows.note: this button should be the full width of the text. can improve the copy to be clear/concise for new users with no context. tagline "folder you keep coming back to" feels a bit like meaningless word salad.

rows.statement: Resume is hidden while there is nothing to resume; once a session exists to resume, the screen is today's again.
rows.note: this is good. i'm also realizing we should probably create a mechanism for users to launch a new session without using a project folder at all. not sure how we'd do this. could be a zero-context/instruction launch, or we could start all users with a new "Home" directory or something that contains some overarching/global assistant settings? maybe just start with a none/zero-context option for now and add the other to roadmap?
